🌍 Iran says inflationary pressures eased in three months to September

📌 Tehran, IRNA – The governor of the Central Bank of Iran (CBI) says inflationary pressures that accelerated sharply after the 40-day war had eased in the three months to September.

Abdolnaser Hemmati said in a post on his personal Telegram channel on Friday that he had discussed Iran’s economic situation in a television interview with Bloomberg on the sidelines of the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund and the World Bank last week.
​
He attributed the sharp acceleration in inflation during the spring to two main factors: a supply shock caused by damage to infrastructure and industrial facilities, and demand-side inflation expectations. Some damaged industrial facilities have returned to production, while central bank monetary tools had helped contain inflation expectations to some extent, he said.
​
Hemmati also said US efforts to isolate Iran economically and tighten the pressure on its economy had failed to achieve their main objective, despite imposing a heavy economic burden on the population.
​
Addressing the impact of lower oil revenues, Hemmati said oil accounted for a limited share of the government’s budget in rial terms. The government planned to cover its budget deficit through other rial-denominated resources, including asset sales, energy-sector reforms and exports of petroleum products.
​
He added that Iran was still receiving foreign currency from oil exports and had made arrangements to address any potential challenges in the future.
​
Hemmati also said the central bank’s reserves were in good condition and could finance the country’s imports until the end of US President Donald Trump’s term and beyond.
​
To help households recover lost purchasing power, he highlighted the government’s commodity voucher program and gradual increases in the rial value of the assistance for low-income families.
